item.text:
**Bottom Line**
The 2023 record is mixed but leans negative for 7B.5. I found clear evidence that Putin still relied on some competent technocrats in economic management, but the stronger pattern in 2023 is loyalist control, secrecy around wealth/conflicts, and at least one direct appointment of a Putin-aligned media insider to a major state post. I did **not** find a reliable 2023 report of Putin appointing a close family member to office.

**Accepted Claims**

- **Official economic decision-making still included technocrats**
  - **Title:** *Совещание по экономическим вопросам* / Meeting on economic issues
  - **Publisher:** President of Russia / Kremlin
  - **Date:** January 17, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://www.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/70364](https://www.special.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/70364)
  - **Claim:** Putin held a formal economic meeting with the government and Central Bank to review key indicators and “concrete measures” for 2023. That is consistent with relying on professional economic administrators rather than replacing them with pure loyalists.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

- **A competent central banker still set an independent line**
  - **Title:** *Russian central bank holds key rate at 7.5%, gives hawkish signal*
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** February 10, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russian-central-bank-holds-key-rate-at-75-gives-hawkish-signal-3000569](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russian-central-bank-holds-key-rate-at-75-gives-hawkish-signal-3000569)
  - **Claim:** Elvira Nabiullina warned about deficit and inflation risks, which is evidence that a professional technocrat still had room to constrain wartime policy pressures.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

- **Technocrats were still debating policy tradeoffs**
  - **Title:** *Russian officials seek to streamline budget spending but disagree on tax hikes*
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** June 15, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/russian-officials-seek-to-streamline-budget-spending-but-disagree-on-tax-hikes-3106392](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/russian-officials-seek-to-streamline-budget-spending-but-disagree-on-tax-hikes-3106392)
  - **Claim:** Finance and economic officials openly debated taxes, spending, and investment effects. That suggests some functioning professional bureaucracy inside the wartime state.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

- **Technocratic restraint appeared in property-rights disputes**
  - **Title:** *Russia should not take temporary control of foreign banks units - central bank*
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** April 28, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russia-should-not-take-temporary-control-of-foreign-banks-units-central-bank-3067714](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/russia-should-not-take-temporary-control-of-foreign-banks-units-central-bank-3067714)
  - **Claim:** Nabiullina opposed a more arbitrary seizure of foreign bank units. This is narrow but real evidence of a professional official pushing back against politicized, insider-driven intervention.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

- **A loyalist was put in charge of state media**
  - **Title:** *Putin ally appointed to head Russia's TASS news agency*
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** May 7, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-ally-appointed-to-head-russias-tass-news-agency-3073207](https://uk.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/putin-ally-appointed-to-head-russias-tass-news-agency-3073207)
  - **Claim:** Putin’s former election spokesman Andrei Kondrashov was appointed to run TASS. That is a direct patronage signal: a trusted political ally, not an outside professional, was elevated to a key propaganda node.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

- **Transparency around personal wealth and conflicts was reduced**
  - **Title:** *Russia ends disclosure rules for officials, citing wartime secrecy needs*
  - **Publisher:** The Washington Post
  - **Date:** February 6, 2023
  - **URL:** [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2023/02/06/russia-corruption-war-ukraine-wagner/](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2023/02/06/russia-corruption-war-ukraine-wagner/)
  - **Claim:** Putin signed legislation exempting lawmakers from full public income and property disclosure. That does not prove a specific appointment choice, but it is strong supporting evidence for a system that tolerates hidden enrichment and weak conflict-of-interest controls.
  - **Question IDs:** 7B.5

**Search Gap**
- I did **not** find a reliable 2023 source showing Putin appointing a close family member to a formal government role.
- The strongest patronage evidence I found is indirect: secrecy around asset disclosure, loyalty-heavy media staffing, and broader deference to security services and political loyalists.
- So the best-supported judgment is: **some technocrats remained in key economic roles, but the overall staffing model still leaned toward loyalism and opacity rather than clean meritocracy.**
